A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SparseDiff research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments on four PDE systems and SEVIR, alongside ablations, noise robustness, generalization, and efficiency analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original forecasting results and adds graph-construction comparisons, sparse-observation experiments, and irregular-mesh wave-equation results.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 changes the reported graph evolution operator from A to A-I, adding a self-subtraction term. Appendix D.1 introduces interpolation and zero-filling for sparse or irregular inputs. The codebook encoder, regional aggregation, diffusion reconstruction, and adaptive re-encoding framework remain.

E1.justification: The original five evaluation systems remain. Appendix D.1 substantially extends input-condition coverage through Navier-Stokes forecasting from only 10% of observed grid points and a new irregular-mesh 2D wave-equation dataset, moving beyond the previously evaluated full regular-grid inputs.

E2.justification: New Section 4.7 and Table 2 evaluate GKN, GRAND with coordinate-based kNN, and GRAND with spectral clustering followed by kNN. These add focused graph-construction comparators; the main ConvLSTM, FNO, UNet, and G-LED comparison set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported diffusion-decoder size changes substantially from 55.21 million parameters in v1 Table 2 to 25.8 million in v2 Table 3, without establishing whether experiments were rerun. New experiments specify 100-step evaluation, kNN neighborhoods containing 20% of probes, and interpolation or zero-filling procedures. Newly disclosed architecture settings alone do not establish changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: Section 4.7 adds a targeted test of region-aware edges against learned and proximity-based graph alternatives. Appendix D.1 adds a missing-observation robustness test on Navier-Stokes. Existing probe-selection, edge-removal, codebook-size, noise, Reynolds-number, and accuracy-efficiency analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 in both versions reports means and standard deviations from 10 runs. No new seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence intervals, or significance tests are introduced. Revised standard-deviation values constitute result changes.

E6.justification: All SparseDiff means and standard deviations in Table 1 change, while baseline entries and rankings remain. For example, Navier-Stokes RMSE changes from 11.390 to 11.130 and Cylinder-Flow from 8.012 to 8.544, in units of 10^-2. Tables 2, 4, and 5 add graph-comparison, sparse-input, and irregular-wave results. These are revised or newly reported outcomes, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The Section 3.2 evolution equation changes from integrating Ah to integrating (A-I)h, also reflected in Figure 2. This changes the mathematical operator rather than merely its notation. Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: sparse spatial encoding, graph-based dynamics, and test-time adaptation through re-encoding. The headline claims of 49.99% error reduction and approximately 1% spatial resolution also remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 retains the edge-weight and averaging limitations, then adds substantive qualifications in Appendix D.1: unreliable interpolation under severe undersampling, computational costs, vulnerability to spatial-layout shifts, and lack of coordinate-querying capabilities. It identifies the UNet decoder as the regular-grid constraint and discusses possible replacements.

D1.justification: New Appendix B supplies previously absent encoder dimensions, lookback length, predictor dimensions, attention heads, RK4 solver, and diffusion architecture settings. The introduction replaces v1's promise of code after review with a stated open-source repository location. These substantially improve the documented implementation and access information.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for the Graph Kernel Network comparison and the irregular wave-equation dataset, cited as references 32 and 47. The existing related-work discussion and overall positioning are otherwise substantially retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order remain. v2 adds focused experimental and architecture subsections, author contributions, acknowledgements, and a conference checklist, alongside local notation explanations, wording corrections, and expanded affiliations. This is a limited extension rather than a broad narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds three experimental tables, relocates and renumbers the parameter table and several figures, updates Figure 2's equation, and reformats the author block. Existing plots and Figure 8's qualitative examples are retained; their relocation does not constitute new experimental evidence.

improvement.justification: The added graph controls, sparse and irregular-input evaluations, architecture details, and explicit applicability limits strengthen validation and reproducibility. The gains are tempered by unexplained reporting differences: v2 Table 1 gives real-world RMSE 7.957 while Figure 3 retains 7.74, both in units of 10^-2, and the substantial decoder-size revision is not explained.
